Capital One.

This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Dave Mattingly.
Democrats and Republicans are still assessing the results of Tuesday's midterm elections
with control of Congress shifting away from the GOP come January.
NPR's Elena Moore says the votes are still being counted in some House and Senate contests.
Democrats have flipped more than two dozen seats in the House, according to race calls
by the Associated Press.
And more are likely, with Democratic candidates up in dozens of additional races that have
yet to be called.
On the Senate side, Democrats have flipped seven seats, with wins in Kansas, Iowa, Maine,
North Carolina, South Carolina, Texas, and Ohio.
A few tight races remain too early to call, notably Alaska and Mississippi.
Alaska was expected to be close.
It was seen as a toss-up race heading into Election Day.
But historically, Ruby Red, Mississippi, was not expected to be this close.
Ballots are still being counted, but the candidates are essentially tied.
Elena Moore, NPR News.
The results of Tuesday's midterm elections will give Democrats a majority of governorships
for the first time in 16 years.
Kentucky's governor, Andy Beshear, chairs the Democratic Governors Association.
He spoke with Sylvia Goodman of Kentucky Public Radio.
Beshear says the election shows Americans want their governors to focus on everyday
needs and repudiate cruelty.
We will not accept leaders who tell us that our neighbor is the enemy from within and
try to push division between us and people we know, simply because they're members of
another party.
He said Americans expect their governors to push back against President Trump, pointing,
for example, to Democrat-led lawsuits over rescinded funding.
Beshear is considered a possible contender for Democratic nominee in 2028 and has hinted
at potential ambitions.
For NPR News, I'm Sylvia Goodman in Louisville, Kentucky.
South Korea is planning to expand its naval mission in the Middle East to include waters
near the Strait of Hormuz.
Still, as NPR's Anthony Kuhn reports from Seoul, South Korea insists it will not be
drawn into the war between the U.S. and Iran.
The South Korean Navy's Chonghe unit has conducted anti-piracy missions in the Gulf
of Aden since 2009.
Its mission will be extended for another year, and its area will be expanded to within about
400 miles of the Strait of Hormuz.
President Trump complained that Seoul had not contributed to the war in Iran when he
scaled back U.S.-South Korean military drills in August aimed at deterring North Korea.
South Korea gets most of its oil through the Strait of Hormuz.
The Chonghe unit's extended deployment is subject to parliamentary approval, and Seoul
has made clear that its mission is to protect South Korean interests and will not involve
any combat operations.
Anthony Kuhn, NPR News, Seoul.
CVS put Aetna in caremark under its one roof in 2018, creating a conglomerate reaching
into many corners of healthcare.
In this marked an era of ballooning healthcare giants, including rivals United Health and
Cigna.
Lately, these companies have faced growing scrutiny from state and federal regulators
and lawmakers over the role in rising health costs.
And the pharmacy business has become tricky with changing drug prices and American spending
habits.
Now, CVS says it's splitting back up.
One company will be the retail pharmacy business.
The other will be Aetna and Caremark doing insurance and pharmacy benefit management.
The announcement says this will help each of the two better focus on their unique goals.
Alina Seluch, NPR News.
For the second time this year, JetBlue says it's raising baggage fees.
The airline says it's doing so to offset higher operating costs, including more expensive
jet fuel.
The fee for a first checked bag is going up from $39 to $50 for most economy passengers
flying within the U.S., Canada, the Caribbean and Latin America.
The airline says that fee will rise to $55 during peak travel periods, including Thanksgiving
and the winter holidays.
The gains on Wall Street yesterday were substantial.
The Dow added 1,569 points, or more than 3 percent.
The S&P gained 1.5 percent.
I'm Dave Mattingly, NPR News, in Washington.
